items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 5 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Only 8.3% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later. Keep it that way: across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 12.0 hours, and 14.3% of nights reached 13 hours. In the randomized program, adding the overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points (95% CI -0.06 to 0.0) compared with coaching alone. It looked larger in some blood sugar groups, but the program could not tell the groups apart, so this is the overall number. A check in real people (NHANES) showed no clear link yet.
